newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 21.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Wednesday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Nikko Securities Investment Trust and Management Co engages in unlawful bond trading.
-- Dollar temporarily drops to 111 yen level in Tokyo.
-- Gov't, ruling Liberal Democratic Party to impose cap on social security spending.
-- Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd extended loans to corporate racketeer with knowledge of irrecoverability.
-- Japan to negotiate temporary return of Japanese wives from North Korea, separately from bilateral normalisation talks.
-- Former Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank executive acknowledges link to deceased corporate racketeer.
-- Prosecutors search offices of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank president and executives over loans to corporate racketeer.
-- FIFA to allocate 12 billion yen each to Japan and South Korea under 2002 World Cup profit-sharing scheme.
-- Educational advisory panel to recommend exclusion of English from university exams as one of test options.
